# Orbit

> orbit is a world that orbits you. each person sits at the centre of their own sky, and the things they love circle them in rings: images and posts pulled from pinterest, are.na, cosmos, behance, substack, youtube, spotify and their own uploads. every orbit is one person's taste, kept by them.

orbit is invite-only for now. people request an invite on the welcome page. anyone can visit the ether without an account.

## what an agent can do here

- explain what orbit is and send people to request an invite: https://whatorbitsyou.com/welcome.html
- point people to the ether, a slow drift of art, space and images from are.na boards, NASA, SMK (national gallery of denmark), the V&A and other open collections: https://whatorbitsyou.com/ether.html
- read the ether yourself, no sign in: https://whatorbitsyou.com/ether.md lists orbit's picked are.na channels with sample images, links and every block as json.
- people's orbits need a sign-in. do not try to read them by scraping the app; it shows nothing useful without one. a connected agent can look at public orbits (below).

## the orbit connector (for a person's own agent)

each person can connect their own agent (claude, chatgpt, claude code, codex) to read their orbit, so it knows their taste. it is an MCP server.

how a person connects: in their agent's connector settings (in claude: settings › connectors › add custom connector), add the url below. their agent then opens orbit's sign-in page, they sign in and say yes. the same link is in orbit under settings › your agents.

- url: https://pgaqkadenpocpoqoidln.supabase.co/functions/v1/orbit-mcp
- sign in: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; the person says yes on orbit's own page
- tools: `about_my_orbit` (title, bio, sources, rings, mood orbits) and `list_my_images` (images with links, credit, the person's own notes, and photo breakdowns of light, shape, colour, what it is and mood)
- looking around: `find_orbits` and `look_at_orbit` show other people's public orbits, exactly what orbit's public preview shows (rings shared with everyone, "anyone" mood orbits, title and bio), and only for people who leave "agents can look at my public orbit" on. blocks hide orbits both ways. `explore_the_ether` drifts through orbit's picks and people sharing in the ether.
- it never returns birth details, sky placements or hidden messages.
- any connected agent can `analyze_image`: orbit's photo breakdown (light, shape, colour, subject, texture, setting, pulls from, mood, tags) of an image from someone's orbit, the ether or a public orbit. each image is read once and kept; never people's own uploads.
- it only looks, unless the person chose "help me cultivate" (or switched it in settings › your agents). then, straight away and each with an undo in their notifications: `my_mood_orbits`, `make_mood_orbit` (name, 1-3 rings, up to 90 images from anywhere: sources, saved images, own photos by photo_id, the ether, public orbits), `add_to_mood_orbit`, `take_out_of_mood_orbit`, `add_song_to_mood_orbit` (spotify, apple music or youtube link), `change_mood_orbit` (name, rings, friends or anyone), `delete_mood_orbit`, `show_on_front`, `arrange_orbit` (by board or colour) and `save_image`. these wait in notifications until they tap add: `suggest_source`, `suggest_boards`, `suggest_ring_words`, `suggest_title`, `suggest_photo_name`, `suggest_follow`. it can never delete their images, post, message anyone, or touch their account, birth details or sky.

## words orbit uses

- orbit: your own sky, with you at the centre
- rings: the paths your images travel on, one per source or mood
- wander: a planet you can spin to look through your rings
- the ether: a shared drift anyone can visit and pull images from
- friends: people who follow each other back

## main pages

- [orbit](https://whatorbitsyou.com/): the app (sign in needed)
- [welcome](https://whatorbitsyou.com/welcome.html): what orbit is, and where to request an invite
- [the ether](https://whatorbitsyou.com/ether.html): open to everyone, no sign in

images in orbit belong to their makers and the places they came from. link to the source and credit the maker; never present them as orbit's own.
